text.p: Biosys Inc., a biotechnology company, said Monday it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection because it has been unable to alleviate a chronic cash shortage.
Biosys' stock plunged 21.9 cents to 12.5 cents on Nasdaq in late morning trading.
The Columbia, Md.-based company said it could not raise the financing necessary to cover losses from poor operating and market conditions.
It previously said cooler and wet weather had depressed its revenues during the second quarter in key market segments and severely reduced available cash resources.
Biosys has posted several quarters of red ink, with losses of $3.6 million on revenues of 6.6 million in the second quarter.
Biosys also said it expected its shares to be delisted from Nasdaq because it was unable to meet exchange requirements of $4 million in net tangible assets or its minimun bid price test.
The company, which filed for reorganization last Friday, said it would operate as a debtor-in-possession and intended to formulate a plan of reorganization or liquidation.
Creditors will receive notice of the filing from the court, it said.
